title: Three-phase motor does not start
faultChecks: Check supply/phase-loss and starter trip status.
Trace STOP, E-stop, overload NC, permissives and coil command.
With isolation confirmed, check winding/insulation and mechanical jam by approved methods.
decision: Coil command absent → controls; contactor operates but no torque → power path, motor or load.

title: Contactor chatters
faultChecks: Check control supply versus coil-rated voltage.
Inspect loose terminals, worn auxiliary seal-in contacts and contactor wear.
Review PLC commands and interlocks for cycling.
decision: Unstable coil voltage → wiring/control source; healthy voltage with chatter → contactor mechanics.

title: Single-phasing / imbalance
faultChecks: Review protection and overload events.
Confirm phase-to-phase supply/load measurements only by authorized methods.
Inspect fuses, contacts, leads and motor after isolation.
decision: Supply missing a phase → upstream; supply normal but load missing → starter/cable.

title: START/STOP seal-in will not latch
faultChecks: Trace series NC stop, overload and process permissives.
Verify NO auxiliary seal-in path and coil voltage.
Inspect reset logic and 2-wire versus 3-wire design.
decision: Runs only while START held → inspect seal-in contact or PLC latch rung.

title: Forward/reverse motor issue
faultChecks: Inspect mutual mechanical and electrical interlocks under isolation.
Trace selected coil and opposite NC auxiliary contact.
Confirm safe direction, feedback and stopping sequence.
decision: Both coils requested → take out of service; never bypass interlocks.

title: ON-delay / OFF-delay replaced incorrectly
faultChecks: Write a timing chart from input transition through output state.
Confirm TON versus TOF, timebase and NO/NC terminal meanings.
Test timing and fail-safe operation using approved procedure.
decision: TON delays energization; TOF delays de-energization.

title: PLC input ON, output OFF
faultChecks: Observe rung from input through every permissive and interlock.
Find the first false instruction and its physical source.
If output rung true, inspect output module power and field wiring.
decision: Rung false → logic/conditions; rung true, no terminal voltage → output stage. Do not force safety I/O.

title: 4–20 mA instrumentation fault
faultChecks: Review loop supply, AI card mode and configured sensor range.
Compare transmitter local indication to loop current and raw PLC value.
Check open loop, polarity, shields and scaling: (mA − 4)/16 × span + minimum.
decision: Correct current, wrong display → scaling; near 0 mA → open loop/supply.

title: VFD overcurrent
faultChecks: Record fault stage: start/accel/steady load/decel.
Inspect ramps, nameplate settings and mechanical binding.
OEM-isolate drive before any cable or motor insulation test.
decision: Start trip → output/cable/motor; loaded trip → torque, process, acceleration.

title: VFD DC-bus overvoltage
faultChecks: Record whether alarm occurs during deceleration.
Review input voltage, ramp, regenerative load and braking design.
OEM-qualified inspection of resistor/chopper and DC bus only.
decision: Deceleration trip → regenerative energy; never access charged DC bus.

title: VFD reversed motor direction
faultChecks: Check commanded direction and drive input assignment.
Confirm safe equipment conditions for a test jog.
Correct motor phasing only with isolation and OEM authorization.
decision: Wrong command → control logic; correct command/wrong rotation → approved motor lead phasing.

title: Battery-electric mining vehicle HV enable
faultChecks: Stop, secure machine, and log BMS/traction/thermal alarms.
Review LV auxiliary supply and safe external permissive diagnostics.
Refer HV isolation, precharge, contactor and battery checks to OEM/site HV-qualified personnel.
decision: Isolation/precharge fault → no bypass; escalate to authorized HV team.

title: Mine sump pump trips
faultChecks: Check level switches, overload/VFD status and discharge obstruction.
Inspect electrical cable/motor after site isolation and moisture precautions.
Evaluate mechanical blockage, dry-run and controller sequence.
decision: No command → level/PLC; high current → hydraulic load or motor.

title: Conveyor E-stop or pull-cord trip
faultChecks: Review exact safety trip and startup sequencing alarms.
Inspect pull-cords, belt drift, zero-speed and chute switches.
Check motor/drive and mechanics only after isolation.
decision: Never bridge safety chain. Correct and verify complete stop/restart sequence.

title: Ventilation fan interlock
faultChecks: Coordinate with mine control; establish approved ventilation state.
Trace airflow/gas/damper/door safety permissives.
Investigate starter, VFD and motor after ruling out safety inhibit.
decision: Life-safety permissive missing → do not bypass; escalate.

title: Feeder relay trip
faultChecks: Record relay element and sequence of events.
Read one-line, coordination settings and affected equipment.
Use switching authorization for downstream fault assessment.
decision: No repeated reclose of unknown fault; investigate phase/ground/overload target.

title: SEL/GE relay or RTU loses SCADA
faultChecks: Separate local protection health from remote telemetry.
Review power, network switch, link, permitted connectivity and alarms.
Check DNP/RTU point mapping, communications and timestamp under change control.
decision: Local data correct/network down → link; link good/points bad → mapping/protocol.

title: Furnace or makeup-air unit lockout
faultChecks: Map call, fan, airflow proof, purge, ignition and flame proving sequence.
Record stage and lockout reason; inspect BAS enable and limits.
Refer combustion/gas train work to properly qualified service personnel.
decision: Never jump flame or pressure safeties; use OEM sequence.

title: Transformer overheating
faultChecks: Compare actual load and temperatures with nameplate and trend.
Review cooling, ventilation, harmonics and phase imbalance.
Qualified inspection of winding/insulation/connection concerns under isolation.
decision: Protection trip or dielectric issue → do not re-energize without investigation.

title: Voltage low only under load
faultChecks: Compare supply and load-end condition at matched load under authorized method.
Review feeder conductor/length and load current.
Inspect high-resistance connections and phase imbalance after isolation.
decision: Normal no-load voltage, low loaded voltage → resistance, undersized run or source capacity.

title: Fire alarm circuit trouble
faultChecks: Identify panel trouble and impacted circuits.
Use authorized impairment and fire-watch controls.
Inspect field wiring supervision, EOL location and device configuration using listed procedures.
decision: Never leave protections disabled; restore and acceptance-test.
